svg.text: FIGURE 3.1: UML USE CASE DIAGRAM — FUNCTIONAL ACTOR BOUNDARIES
Functional Decomposition across Core Practice Arena, Real-Time 1v1 Battle Arena, and Administrative Governance Subsystems

g.text: SKILL BATTLE PLATFORM — SYSTEM BOUNDARY
18 TOTAL USE CASES
1. Authentication & Algorithmic Practice Arena (UC-01 to UC-07)
UC-01: Register & Authenticate Account (JWT & HttpOnly)
UC-02: Manage User Profile & Developer Preferences
UC-03: Browse Problem Library by Topic Tag Chips
UC-04: Filter Challenges by Difficulty & Acceptance Rate
UC-05: Write Code in Monaco Editor (JS / Python)
UC-06: Execute Sample Tests in AST In-Memory Sandbox
UC-07: Submit Final Solution & Evaluate Hidden Tests
Practice Subsystem Architectural Scope:
• Provides isolated algorithmic training ground with immediate runtime feedback.
• Employs regex AST parsing to neutralize unsafe Node.js/Python system calls before VM invocation.
• Automatically caches code draft in scoped localStorage keys to prevent accidental loss across reloads.
• Persists submission records with execution latency (ms), memory footprint (MB), and testcase pass ratio.
2. Real-Time 1v1 Battle Arena & Gamification (UC-08 to UC-14)
UC-08: Create 1v1 Battle Lobby & 6-Char Room Code
UC-09: Join Battle Lobby with 6-Character Room Code
UC-10: Compete in Synchronized 1v1 Duel Match
UC-11: Stream Opponent Testcase Progress Live
UC-12: View 365-Day Activity Heatmap & Streaks
UC-13: Solve 24-Hour Deterministic Daily Challenge
UC-14: View Global Leaderboards & ELO Badges
Multiplayer Subsystem Architectural Scope:
• Full-duplex Socket.IO WebSocket synchronization over dedicated /battle namespace.
• Server-authoritative state clock enforcing 3-second ready countdown and 15-minute game termination.
• Live telemetry broadcasting passing testcase counts to opponents without revealing raw source code.
• Atomic ELO rating updates: +100 points for first-to-solve victory, -25 for defeat (floor 800), +25 for draw.
• Daily Challenge engine delivers rotating algorithmic puzzles every 24 hours awarding 50 bonus rating points.
3. Platform Governance & Infrastructure Telemetry (UC-15 to UC-18)
UC-15: Monitor Real-Time System Telemetry & Load
UC-16: Problem CRUD (Author Statements & Test Suites)
UC-17: Student Governance & Account Suspension
UC-18: Schedule Deterministic Daily Challenge Calendar
Administrative Governance Subsystem Scope:
• Privileged administrative operations protected by RBAC middleware verifying JWT role claims.
• Full CRUD capability for curriculum problems: markdown description formatting, constraints, tags, testcase suite generation.
• Moderation engine allows instant suspension of compromised accounts with immediate token invalidation via TTL blacklist.
• Automated telemetry monitoring tracking active WebSocket connections, CPU usage, and database query latency.
• Controls daily challenge schedule to ensure equitable competitive scheduling and bonus point allocation.
👤 STUDENT ACTOR
Primary Platform Participant:
• Initiates practice sessions
• Solves algorithmic problems
• Competes in 1v1 duels
• Earns rating points & badges
• Participates in daily events
Associated Use Cases:
• UC-01 through UC-07 (Core)
• UC-08 through UC-14 (Battle)
Security Context:
• Access: Public & Authenticated
• Token Claims: role: 'student'
• Rate Limited: 100 req/15min
🛡️ ADMIN ACTOR
Platform Governance Authority:
• Authors problem test suites
• Manages challenge calendar
• Inspects system telemetry
• Enforces academic integrity
• Suspends delinquent users
Associated Use Cases:
• UC-01 (Admin Login)
• UC-15 through UC-18 (Governance)
Security Context:
• Access: RBAC Admin Gate
• Token Claims: role: 'admin'
• Audit Logged: Every mutation
UML USE CASE MODELING CONVENTIONS & RELATIONS:
Core Practice Arena: Algorithmic problem discovery, editing & AST execution
Battle Arena: 1v1 multiplayer duels, WebSockets, ELO ratings & daily challenges
Governance: System telemetry, problem CRUD, and student account moderation
Security Perimeter: Role-based access control with JWT revocation checking
Boundary Specification: All interactions within the boundary box represent automated system services executed by the Node.js/Express server and MongoDB.
